## Summary

The 17 Nov five-preview audit found that the palletizer robot cell's full floor slab inherited `safetyPaint`. It now has a separate `concrete` control and preset colors; the fence posts and robot pedestal retain safety paint. Geometry and triangle budget are unchanged.

This branch also contains the preceding industrial-plant material corrections for the roller conveyor, steam manifold, scrubber, inline flow meter, reactor vessel, and process blower.

## Verification

- Focused exported-GLB material regression: 1/1 passed.
- ESLint on the industrial-plant kit and new test: clean.
- `catalog/index.json` regenerated; the diff contains only the palletizer row and its source SHA matches the source. Preview path exists.
- Industrial-plant quality gate: 60/60 (100%). Global quality scan: 2,398/2,402 (99.83%); four unchanged `standard-components` files fail the material-count rule and match `origin/develop`.
- Five reviewed previews, before/after source and PNGs, MP4 demo, settings, and verification evidence: [handoff bundle](artifacts/catalog-demos/palletizer-robot-cell-floor-material-review-20261117/README.md).

The branch is not deployed. The demo shows local source editing, software-rendered previews, and a GLB regression only; it is not simulation or hardware acceptance.



## Latest round — scissor lift table arm finishes (2026-11-17)

The five-preview audit selected `industrial-plant/scissor-lift-table`: its matched `scissor-arm-b` parts used `safetyPaint`, while the corresponding `scissor-arm-a` parts used `steel`. Both B arms now use the existing `steel` control; geometry, parameters, presets, and the 196-triangle mesh are unchanged.

- The GLB material regression fails on the original source and passes after the correction (1/1).
- Regenerated the scissor-lift preview and `catalog/index.json`; the generated diff changes only this asset row and its source hash.
- ESLint is clean. Industrial-plant quality: 60/60 (100%). Global structural quality: 2,398/2,402 (99.83%); the four unchanged exceptions are in `standard-components`.
- Full catalog integration passes: 141 files / 211 tests, including the index freshness check.
- [Five-preview ledger, before/after preview, source snapshots, verification, and inspected 14-second MP4](artifacts/catalog-demos/industrial-plant-scissor-lift-table-arm-material-review-20261117/README.md).

The current public detail page and old preview returned HTTP 200 before this update, with the live preview matching the baseline image. This branch is not deployed; the new preview has not been verified on the deployed page. The MP4 shows a local source edit, software-rendered preview, and GLB regression only; it is not simulation or hardware acceptance.
title: fix(catalog): refine industrial-plant material finishes

body:
## Summary

`examples/gallery/ratchet-stool.kcad.ts` now passes the physics-grounded loop with `mechanism: real` and no failures. Before this change it gave `mechanism: broken` with 119 mechanism failures. This closes the gap that issue #351 tracked with an `it.skip` citation.

## Reproduction (origin/develop fc764c2f0)

`runValidateCli({ file, includeInterference: true, epsilon: 0.01, physical: false, includePhysics: false, json: true })` reported failures at the `rest`, `height-adjust:0` and `height-adjust:34` poses:

- The inner post and rack sat inside a solid outer sleeve (47.49 mm³) and the collar. Neither part had a bore or a rack slot.
- Each ratchet tooth was sunk 4 mm into the rack backer.
- The pawl pivot boss, nose and spring sat in the path of the rack teeth.
- Each leg end was 3 mm inside its foot pad (2.80 mm³ each).
- Each foot-ring strut ended on the ring centre line.
- `mechanism.mate-gap`: the foot ring was 5.88 mm from the sleeve it was mated to, and the lever was 1.22 mm from its pivot boss.

## Change

Model source only (`examples/gallery/ratchet-stool.kcad.ts`). All part names are unchanged.

- The sleeve has a bore for the post (0.5 mm clearance). The sleeve and the split collar have a slot for the rack.
- The teeth are welded edge-on to the rack face. Their position is calculated from the tooth length, thickness and tilt.
- The pawl group moves to the -Y side of the rack. The boss rests on the collar, and the lever is tangent to the boss. The nose extends from the lever side face into the gap between teeth 4 and 5. The spring stands on the collar under the lever.
- The travel is now 4 × the 8 mm rack pitch (32 mm; it was 34 mm). The nose sits in a tooth gap at both travel limits.
- The legs end on the pad tops, and the struts end on the inner face of the ring. The foot ring is mated to a strut, not to the sleeve.

## Tests

- `tests/integration/examples/ratchetStool.test.ts`: the `it.skip` is replaced by a real `runValidateCli` regression that expects `mechanism: 'real'` and `mechanismFailures: []`.
- `exampleSweepShared.ts`: the example moves from `ISSUE_TRACKED` to `HOSTED_IN_DEDICATED_FILE` (`run-validate-cli`).

Results:

- `npx vitest run tests/integration/examples/ratchetStool.test.ts tests/integration/physics-loop/exampleSweepGate.test.ts`: 2 files and 6 tests pass (12 s).
- The same validate call on the old model gives `mechanism: broken` with 119 failures.
- `typecheckExamples` on this file: 15 errors, which is the same count as the original model on develop (existing loose connector and colour typing). No error is new.
- `render inspect` iso and front views were inspected. The legs stand on the pads, the teeth stand on the rack face, the lever rests on the boss, the knob sits on the lever, and the struts carry the foot ring.

## Notes

- This PR probably conflicts in `exampleSweepShared.ts` with #1400 (meta-glasses). Both PRs remove adjacent `ISSUE_TRACKED` entries. The resolution is to keep both removals and both `HOSTED_IN_DEDICATED_FILE` entries.
- Limitation: the pose sweep checks only the travel limits. A real ratchet lifts its pawl between detents, and this static model does not represent that.

## Summary

`examples/gallery/meta-glasses.kcad.ts` still failed the physics-grounded loop. Issue #350 tracked this failure and was closed on 2026-09-18 without a fix. The example was skip-tracked in `ISSUE_TRACKED`, so CI did not see the failure. This PR fixes the geometry and replaces the skip with a real regression test.

## Reproduction (origin/develop 3713bdda0)

`runValidateCli({ file, includeInterference: true, epsilon: 0.01, physical: false, includePhysics: false })` → `mechanism: broken`, 6 failures:

| Pair | Shared volume | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| frame / left and right temple | 73.83 mm³ each | temple front block starts 4 mm inside the frame back |
| temple / hinge barrel, left and right | 103.04 mm³ each | barrel inside a solid temple |
| camera bezel / camera glass | 12.45 mm³ | bezel is a solid disc |
| right temple / touch strip | 18.00 mm³ | strip 0.15 mm into the temple |

## Change

- Start the temple front block at the frame back face (Y = `FRAME_DEPTH / 2`).
- Bore the temple for the hinge barrel.
- Make the camera bezel a ring around the glass.
- Recess the touch strip into the right temple, so its face is still flush.
- `metaGlasses.test.ts`: replace the `it.skip(... issues/350)` with a `runValidateCli` test that requires `mechanism: real` and no failures.
- `exampleSweepShared.ts`: move the example from `ISSUE_TRACKED` to `HOSTED_IN_DEDICATED_FILE` (`run-validate-cli`).

## Results

- After the change: `mechanism: real`, 0 failures.
- The new test fails on the old model with `mechanism.interpenetration` and passes on the new model.
- `npx vitest run tests/integration/examples/metaGlasses.test.ts tests/integration/physics-loop/exampleSweepGate.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- `exampleParseSmoke` filtered to `meta-glasses`: 9 passed.
- ESLint on the 3 changed files: clean. `scripts/typecheckExamples.ts`: no new errors (the existing implicit-`any` warnings in this file move by 3 lines).
- `kernelcad render inspect` (front, right, top and iso): the temples now start at the back face of the frame, the hinge-barrel ends show on top of the temple blocks, the touch strip shows on the right temple, and the bezel and LED show on the front. No parts are missing or detached. No MP4: this PR changes example geometry, not a feature or tool.

## Not in scope

The other skip-tracked examples still report `mechanism: broken` on develop. Their issues are also closed: ratchet-stool (#351, 119 failures), compact-supported-arm (#346, 6), desktop-3axis-mates (#347, 9) and skill-built-supported-arm (#352, 6).

body:
## Summary

Rebuilds `examples/robot-arm/compact-supported-arm.kcad.ts` in place as a manufacturable desktop 4-DOF arm: a turntable base, envelope-level purchased actuators in printed pockets, filleted box and I-section links, horns and hinge pins, and a two-finger compound gripper. The six revolute mates stay in order (`base-yaw`, `shoulder-pitch`, `elbow-pitch`, `grip`, `left-curl`, `right-curl`), and the parameter names, defaults, and ranges are unchanged. The first part is still `base-plate`. Finger pads were added as `left-finger-pad` and `right-finger-pad`.

The gripper uses module 0.6 trapezoid teeth (19/38 external and 57/114 internal) on a 17.1 mm centre. Tip circles are held 0.25 mm apart so a curl sampled apart from the grip does not collide. The pinions are mesh-side sectors on root disks so the swept-collision face budget still reports the mechanism as real. No custom collision proxies and no moving ignore-pairs.

Please review the rendered look before merge. Local previews are in the review bundle, not in this PR.

## Verification

- `evaluate` — ok, 0 errors, 6.73 s real
- `evaluate --envelope --samples-per-mate 2 --combinatorial` — ok, 77 samples, 0 envelope diagnostics, 10.19 s real
- `validate --include-interference --physical --include-physics` — ok, mechanism `real`, 19 parts, 18 joints, 13.08 s real
- swept collision — ok, 270 poses, 0 collisions, 85.71 s real together with physics. Four sample-density warnings (shoulder-pitch, grip, left-curl, right-curl) do not fail the check. Physics verify — ok, mechanism `real`
- `compactSupportedArm.test.ts` — 3 passed, 34.56 s real (inspect 4.6 s, review 19.4 s). The two previously skipped checks pass unchanged and are re-enabled. The issue 346 sweep mapping is removed.
- `robotArmVerifyAssembly.test.ts` — 3 passed, 13.38 s real
- `livePhysicsPoses.test.ts` — 3 passed, 41.19 s real
- `exampleParseSmoke.test.ts -t compact-supported-arm` — passed, 2.52 s real. The example stays HEAVY because a 6.7 s evaluate exceeds the 4.5 s smoke budget.
- `exampleSweepGate.test.ts` — passed after the mapping change

## Test plan

- [ ] Look at the default pose and the yawed open-grip pose before merge
- [ ] Confirm the mechanism verdict stays `real` on CI
- [ ] Do not merge until the look is accepted
title: Rebuild the compact supported arm as a desktop 4-DOF

body:
## What

Two commits: the second needs the first.

**1. Dependency-aware incremental rebuild** (`computeGraphReuse`, `rebuildModelIncremental`)

Before, cached shapes were reused only when the new script was a pure append of the old one. Now every record the edit provably did not touch is seeded. A record is reused when all of these hold:
- same id;
- healthy cached shape in the previous build;
- identical resolved structural hash;
- every input it consumes was itself reused.

Dependencies follow the same input edges the engine and `affectedFeatureIds` already use. A changed feature re-lowers itself and its downstream, nothing else. When nothing is reusable, it falls back to a full build.

**2. Plain JS math on `param()` values**

`param('w', 60) + 4`, `w / 2`, `Math.tan(a * Math.PI / 180)`, loops and point lists now work inside a script. Before, numeric coercion threw. The Oct 3 usage triage showed users writing `.add/.multiply` chains and placeholder workarounds.

How it works:
- **Coercion is bound per session.** `param()` binds each numeric `ParamRef` to its capture session through a `WeakMap`, so record serialization and structural hashes are unchanged. Derived refs inherit the binding. Coercion returns the current value and records the param in `session.coercedParams`. Unbound refs still throw.
- **`updateModelParams`.** An edit to a coerced param writes the new default into the source (`setParamValue`) and rebuilds through `model.rebuildFromSource`, which is (1). Only features whose inputs changed are lowered. The model object is refreshed in place, because animation, warm sessions and publish measurement hold it. Validation and failure semantics are unchanged, and non-coerced params keep the in-place path.
- **`diff_geometry`.** Overrides that name a coerced param rewrite the source and re-run, instead of re-lowering stale records.
- **Skill docs** (`kernelcad-params`, `kernelcad-authoring`) now teach plain math alongside the symbolic methods.

## Evidence (`docs/demos/params-plain-math/`)

52-feature plate with 24 holes, plus a tab angled by `Math.tan(tabAngle…)`. Local run:

| Step | Time | Re-lowered / reused |
|---|---:|---|
| `tabAngle` 30 → 45 | 204 ms | 2 / 50 |
| `tabAngle` 45 → 60 | 152 ms | 2 / 50 |
| Full rebuild | 2226 ms | 52 |

Heights are exact (24 mm and 38.641 mm). The bundle has `bench.ts`, `bench-output.jsonl`, three renders, inspected frames and a 16 s `demo.mp4`.

## Verification
- `tests/unit/kernel/buildModel.test.ts`:
  - mid-script edit reuses the unrelated box and fillet (object-identical) and matches a full build;
  - no-op edit lowers nothing;
  - coerced `updateModelParams` 60→100→30 gives 104/34 mm, never re-lowers the unrelated box/fillet, keeps model identity, rejects out-of-range values.
- `paramRefArithmetic.test.ts`: bound coercion (operators, `Math.*`, derived refs, names recorded).
- `paramArithmeticDiagnostic.test.ts`: the #439 repro now builds.
- `diffGeometry.test.ts`: plain-math resize. It fails without the fix (stale 280 mm³).
- Related suites (skills, scripts/ratchets, modeling, composition, kernel, runtime, capture, mcp tools): 2,618 passed; the 1 failure is `importStep` failed-write, a pre-existing root-container issue.
- Full suite on commit 1: the same 7 environmental failures as `develop` (CLI bundle needs `dist/`, importStep root, MAX30102, NURBS ×2).

Studio sliders and the hosted MCP get this after the server/app pick up this kernel version.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01GcwWN7VzMJRZnceko1mrEk

## Backlog triage — 2026-11-03

Returning to draft after full production-diff review found a correctness regression not covered by the green tests. With `w=param('w',60)`, `t=param('t',5)` and `box(w+4,30,t)`, editing t to 10 through the symbolic path then w to 80 through source rewrite rebuilds from stale `model.code` and restores t to 5. Preserve all current parameter values during source rewriting and add this mixed-path sequential-edit regression. The replacement session/engine must also preserve `onRelower` subscriptions and emit the expected notification; the new path currently does neither. Do not merge until these behaviors are covered and current-head CI passes.
title: feat(params): plain JS math on params, fast and universal (dependency-aware rebuild)

body:
## What
`internalSpurGear` now builds the ring as **one sketch with two loops** (the rim circle is the outer loop and the tooth-bore outline is a hole), extruded once. Before, it extruded a cylinder and then subtracted an extruded bore. On the XY extrude path, multi-loop NURBS profiles now build a holed face through `buildNurbsProfileOnPlane` (replicad `CompoundSketch`). Before, that path accepted a single loop only.

## Measured (.perf harness, local, same machine)
| | before (develop) | after |
|---|---|---|
| 54 T m1 ring alone, cold (incl. init) | 7.4 s | 0.7 s |
| planetary-gearbox warm build | 13.1 s | 2.87 s |
| GT2 shop-release actuator warm build (same model file both sides) | 9.49 s | 2.02 s |
| planetary mesh | ~0.92 s | ~0.92 s (unchanged) |

## Geometry
- 54 T ring: volume 3767.810 → 3767.817 mm³ (+1.9e-6 relative); area +1.8e-6 relative; bounds identical.
- Faces 327 → 328: the rim is now two half-cylinders.
- Selectors on a 12 T ring:
  - cutout on `'top'`: 1019.152 vs 1019.151 mm³
  - fillet on `'bottom'`: identical (1021.355)
  - chamfer `'top'`: failed before, now works (1017.644)

## ⚠️ HOLD: do not merge without review
This changes face IDs, and one selector gives different geometry:
- Face refs change owner from `boolean_1` to `extrude_1`. `'top'`/`'bottom'` lose their stored history lineage but still resolve geometrically.
- The rim splits into 2 faces.
- **`shell(0.8, 'top')` on a ring differs: 371.8 vs 650.8 mm³, and the bounds break (~100 s).**

Saved models that reference ring-gear face IDs, or that shell a ring, may change.

## Tests
`tests/unit/modeling/internalSpurGearHoledExtrude.test.ts` has 2 tests (~1.9 s):
- volume, bounds and plane faces, with no boolean record
- the `'top'`/`'bottom'` selectors still work

typecheck, lint and qualityRatchet pass locally. The wide vitest run shows only the known env-only failures (parts catalog, CLI bundle, nurbs corpus), the same as develop.
title: perf(gears): ring gear as one holed-profile extrude (HOLD: face IDs change)
